claim: A ballot measure was submitted in November 2025 to increase penalties for fentanyl-related offenses in Colorado's 2026 general election.
evidence: A coalition submitted over 200,000 signatures to place the measure on the 2026 ballot to increase penalties for fentanyl manufacturing, distribution, and possession.
source_title: GOP-backed ballot measure would make any fentanyl possession a felony in Colorado
limitations: Information based on media reports from 2025; ballot outcomes and future legislative changes unknown.

claim: The measure proposes making possession of any amount of fentanyl a felony and manufacturing/distributing fentanyl a Class 1 felony with up to 32 years imprisonment.
evidence: Measure classifies the sale of fentanyl as Class 1 felony with prison up to 32 years, and possession of any amount as felony.
source_title: Colorado ballot measure for tougher fentanyl penalties moves forward - Colorado Politics
limitations: Details subject to final wording and legal interpretation; based on media summaries.
